topStories.headline: Midlothian Voters Reject All Five Bond Propositions by Wide Margins
topStories.dek: Every piece of the $192.45 million bond package went down on November 3, with the largest proposition losing by roughly 62 to 38 percent.
topStories.body:
Midlothian voters turned away the city's entire 2026 bond package on Tuesday, November 3, defeating all five propositions by double-digit margins. Proposition A, the largest at $102.3 million for street and road improvements, drew the closest result — still losing 62 to 38 percent. The remaining four propositions, covering a new police substation ($6.81M), drainage projects ($10M), existing park upgrades ($47.26M), and two new parks ($26.09M), all failed by wider spreads, with the police substation proposal drawing the least support at roughly 31 percent in favor.

The package had been championed by city staff as a means to address Midlothian's rapid growth — the population now exceeds 47,000 — and the city argued that its strong financial position allowed it to take on the debt without raising the tax rate. A citizens planning committee recommended the five-year program after reviewing the city's roads, parks, and infrastructure needs.

With 100 percent of precincts reporting, unofficial results were posted to the city's election page. Results remain unofficial until formally canvassed by Ellis County. City Council has not yet indicated whether any propositions will return to voters in a future election cycle.

The defeat leaves several projects in limbo, particularly long-discussed road improvements and the police substation proposed to serve Midlothian's expanding southern areas. The scale of the rejection — none of the five propositions cleared 38 percent — will likely prompt city leadership to revisit both the projects themselves and the approach used to build public support for them.

topStories.headline: Red Oak Hawks Make History in First 6A Season, Head to Bi-District Playoffs
topStories.dek: Playing the toughest district in Texas for the first time ever, Red Oak finished 6-3 and faces Killeen Harker Heights in the first round on November 13.
topStories.body:
Red Oak High School's football program is headed to the UIL playoffs in its inaugural Class 6A season — a milestone for a school and community that have grown rapidly in recent years. The Hawks finished the regular season 6-3 overall and 4-2 in District 11-6A, one of the most competitive districts in the state, which includes Duncanville, North Crowley, Waxahachie, and Mansfield.

Red Oak officially moved into UIL Class 6A District 11 for the 2026-2028 athletic seasons following a realignment announced in February. Head coach Melvin Robinson, in his fourth season, guided the team through a demanding schedule. Key wins over Mansfield (23-20 on the road), Crowley (29-28 away), and Lake Ridge (41-38 away) secured the playoff berth despite lopsided losses to Duncanville and Waxahachie.

The Hawks' first-round bi-district game is set for 7 p.m. Friday, November 13, at Leo Buckley Stadium in Killeen, where they will face Killeen Harker Heights. It is the program's first-ever Class 6A playoff game.

The season also coincides with the district's preparation for a brand-new football stadium, adding further momentum to what Red Oak ISD has described as a new era for Hawk Athletics and the broader community.

topStories.headline: H.A. Wooden Elementary Earns U.S. News 'Best Elementary School' Designation
topStories.dek: The Red Oak ISD campus ranks first in the district and in the top 40 percent of Texas elementary schools in the 2027 U.S. News rankings.
topStories.body:
H.A. Wooden Elementary School in Red Oak has been recognized as a U.S. News Best Elementary School in the publication's 2027 rankings, landing at No. 1 among all elementary campuses in Red Oak ISD and within the top 40 percent of ranked elementary schools statewide. The school serves pre-K through fifth grade and enrolls roughly 524 students at 200 Louise Ritter Boulevard in Red Oak.

U.S. News data show that Wooden outperformed its district peers in both math and reading proficiency on state assessments — 54 percent of students scored at or above proficiency in math and 57 percent in reading. The campus ranked No. 1,331 among the 4,437 Texas elementary schools evaluated.

Red Oak ISD announced the recognition on its district website. The honor arrives during a stretch of broader district momentum: the district also received designation as a CTE District of Distinction by the Career and Technical Association of Texas for the second consecutive year, and its overall state accountability score rose from 77 in 2025 to 78 in 2026, with the number of academic distinctions climbing from seven to ten.

moreNews.headline: Public Comment on Midlothian Limestone Trail Segments 2 & 3 Closes November 13
moreNews.body: The City of Midlothian and TxDOT are seeking written public feedback on Segments 2 and 3 of the proposed Limestone Trail, which would extend the route from Shady Grove Road to Trail Bridge No. 6. An in-person open house was held at Midlothian City Hall on October 29; an identical virtual version of the meeting remains accessible online. All comments must be received by Friday, November 13, 2026. The Limestone Trail is designed to provide a safe pedestrian and cycling corridor connecting neighborhoods, parks, and businesses along the Waxahachie Creek corridor.

moreNews.headline: Red Oak Posts Notice of Intent to Issue Certificates of Obligation
moreNews.body: The City of Red Oak has posted a Notice of Intention to Issue Certificates of Obligation, timed to its November 9 City Council meeting. The move aligns with the capital financing plan the council approved at its August 17 meeting as part of the FY2026-27 budget, which included roughly $35 million in certificates of obligation to fund roadway improvements, utility projects, and carryover capital work. That budget package passed on a 4-0 council vote.
